key_concept: Identifying the characteristic internal membrane structures of cell organelles: cristae in mitochondria, cisternae in the Golgi, thylakoids in chloroplasts, and phospholipids as the main lipid of the cell membrane.
steps: A. Cristae: the inner mitochondrial membrane folds inward into the matrix, forming cristae, which increase the surface area. So A matches II.
B. Cisternae: the Golgi apparatus is made of flat, disc-shaped sacs called cisternae, about $0.5\,\mu m$ to $1.0\,\mu m$ in diameter, stacked parallel to each other. So B matches IV.
C. Thylakoids: flattened membranous sacs lying in the stroma of the chloroplast. They are stacked like coins to form grana. So C matches I.
D. Phospholipid: the major lipid of the cell (plasma) membrane, arranged as a bilayer in the fluid mosaic model. So D matches III.
The correct combination is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III, which is option (2).
why_not_others: Option (1) gives cristae to the cell membrane, and option (4) swaps cristae with cisternae; both also wrongly pair phospholipid with mitochondrial infoldings. Option (3) correctly matches A and B but wrongly links thylakoids to the cell membrane and phospholipids to chloroplast sacs.
common_trap: Students confuse 'cristae' (mitochondria) with 'cisternae' (Golgi or ER) because the two words sound alike.
time_saving_tip: Fix the surest pair first, A-II (cristae are mitochondrial infoldings). Only options (2) and (3) remain, and D-III (phospholipid in the cell membrane) picks option (2).
